definition: Forlorn means lonely, hopeless, or wearing the pitiful look of abandonment.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word forlorn. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know forlorn should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: A single forlorn beach umbrella stood open in the November drizzle, weeks after the concession stand had closed.
Lonely is milder than forlorn — a lonely evening passes, while forlorn adds abandonment and the sense that no one is coming.
Godforsaken goes further than forlorn — so utterly abandoned that even the hope of rescue feels absurd.

Abandoned states the bare fact of being left behind — an owner gone, a claim given up — and says nothing about how the thing looks. Forlorn adds the pitiable air: lonely, hopeless, wearing its desertion openly. The fact is abandonment; the heartbreaking look of it is forlorn.

Dejected means downcast after a particular disappointment — a lost match, a rejected application — and it belongs to people and their moods. Forlorn can settle on anything: a mitten, a platform, a person, each wearing the same lonely, hopeless look of being left behind. Dejection follows an event; forlornness is an air.

By Friday the last stall in the emptied market looked forlorn: one crate of apples, a hand-lettered sign, and an owner who had stopped calling out to shoppers who never came.

Forlorn is more than 'alone.' It bundles three things — loneliness, abandonment, and a hopeless air — and it works as well for things as for people, which is why a single mitten on a fence can be forlorn.
Forlorn paints lonely abandonment with a brush of hopelessness, and it works as well for objects and places as for people — a forlorn mitten, a forlorn platform at midnight.
'Lonely' names a feeling; forlorn paints the whole picture.
Beside its unit-mates: bereft misses one precious thing, abject has lost even dignity — forlorn is the look of being left behind.

At the far end of the bus depot stands the city's last payphone, and nobody has fed it a coin since spring.
It is a forlorn sight: the receiver hangs slightly crooked, the metal cord is furred with dust, and the little light above the keypad still blinks for customers who never come.
The depot itself is busy — riders stream past it all day, phones in their hands.
A maintenance sheet taped inside the booth shows the last service visit was canceled.
No repair, the note says, is scheduled.
A columnist wrote that the booth looks like it is waiting for one final call, and that the waiting is the saddest part.
